title: Equations and Inequalities
lines: USAT asks about 3 questions on equations: linear equations, pairs of simultaneous equations, quadratics and inequalities, often wrapped in a short word problem. The key skill is turning words into an equation quickly, then solving it with as little arithmetic as possible.
## Linear equations
- Do the same thing to both sides. Clear fractions first by multiplying by the LCM of the denominators; clear decimals by multiplying by 10 or 100.
- Expand brackets carefully: −3(x − 2) = −3x + 6.
- Check your answer by putting it back into the original equation. It takes ten seconds and catches most slips.
## Simultaneous equations
- Elimination: add or subtract the equations so one letter disappears. If 3x + 2y = 16 and 5x − 2y = 16, adding gives 8x = 32.
- Substitution: make one letter the subject (y = 2x − 1) and put it into the other equation.
- Shortcut for symmetric pairs: if 4a + 3b = 260 and 3a + 4b = 230, adding gives 7(a + b) = 490, so a + b = 70, and subtracting gives a − b = 30.
- Two lines ax + by = c have no solution when their x and y coefficients are in the same ratio but the constants are not (parallel lines).
## Quadratic equations
- Rearrange to ax² + bx + c = 0, then factorise or use x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] / 2a.
- Never divide both sides by x: x² = 5x gives x(x − 5) = 0, so x = 0 or 5.
- Sum of roots = −b/a; product of roots = c/a. Then α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ.
- The discriminant b² − 4ac tells the nature of the roots: positive means two real roots, zero means equal roots, negative means no real roots. A perfect square gives rational roots.
- An equation with roots p and q is x² − (p + q)x + pq = 0.
## Inequalities
- Solve like an equation, but reverse the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative number: −2x > 6 gives x < −3.
- Double inequalities: do the same thing to all three parts. −1 < 2x + 3 ≤ 9 gives −2 < x ≤ 3.
- Quadratic inequalities: find the roots, then (x − a)(x − b) < 0 between the roots, > 0 outside them.
- x² < 25 means −5 < x < 5, not just x < 5.
## Turning words into equations
| Words | Equation
| a number increased by 7 | x + 7
| 5 less than twice a number | 2x − 5
| A is 3 times as old as B | A = 3B
| in 6 years' time | add 6 to every age
| two-digit number with digits a and b | 10a + b
- The 'all of one kind' trick for coin and ticket problems: assume every item is the cheaper kind, then each expensive item adds the price difference.
## Worked examples
> A purse holds 40 notes of Rs 10 and Rs 50, worth Rs 1,200. How many Rs 50 notes are there?
> If all 40 were Rs 10 notes, they would make Rs 400. Each Rs 50 note adds Rs 40 more. 1,200 − 400 = 800, so there are 800 ÷ 40 = 20 Rs 50 notes.
> Bushra is 5 times as old as her son. In 6 years she will be 3 times as old. Find the son's age.
> Solve x² − 2x − 15 < 0.
> (x − 5)(x + 3) < 0, so the expression is negative between the roots: −3 < x < 5.
! Dividing by a variable loses solutions. Factorise instead.
! Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses the sign. Forgetting this is the most common inequality error.
! Read what is asked. Many word problems set x as one quantity and then ask for another (the father, not the son; the notebook, not the pen).
## Quick check
- Can you write the sum and product of the roots of 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0? (7/2 and 3/2)
- Do you flip the sign when dividing an inequality by −3?
- Can you set up an age problem in one line?
